items.summary: Kelvin Hong spent seven years in Singapore's civil service, where he worked on economic policy including writing the first government paper on fighting SARS, before leaving to pursue entrepreneurship. He sold his condominium unit and moved his family of five from a rental property down to an HDB resale flat while funding his businesses through uncertain times. In 2010, he sold his chain of wellness outlets for what was described as a multimillion-dollar business, later calling the decision his best financial move because it gave him time to reset spiritually and rebuild tuition ventures on a smaller scale. He founded The Economics Tutor in 1998 while running other businesses, has accumulated about 28 years teaching economics, holds a first-class honours Bachelor of Social Sciences from the National University of Singapore, and now runs both The Economics Tutor and Ace GP Tuition alongside his wife. On investments, he prefers building businesses over stocks—keeping savings in safe assets rather than chasing high prices—and views his children's education as his most certain investment while planning to invest a hypothetical $1 million windfall mostly in tuition costs with the rest held in T-bills.
items.title: Singapore Entrepreneur Trades Iron Rice Bowl for Business Ventures and Tuition Focus

items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who will co-chair the 22nd Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation with Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang in Singapore on November 23, argues that the long-standing Singapore-China economic relationship can be deepened through shared innovation. He frames this view as a policy proposal rather than an established fact, noting that both economies have pursued significant investment in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and biotechnology. As supporting evidence for existing collaboration, he cites Enterprise Singapore's Co-Innovation Programmes with Chinese provinces and cities launched in 2020, which by the time of writing had supported more than 40 projects across AI, biomedical sciences, and green technologies; the China-Singapore Guangzhou Knowledge City established in 2010 as a platform for commercialising innovations within China's Greater Bay Area; and the Singapore-China Science and Technology People-To-People Exchange Programme launched at the 19th JCBC in 2023. He also points to concrete deployments, such as self-driving shuttle services introduced by Grab and ComfortDelGro with Chinese technology firms WeRide and Pony.ai in Punggol town, though he presents these as illustrative rather than quantified achievements. Gan positions the upcoming meeting primarily as an opportunity to announce further cooperation agreements between research centres; all stated figures are attributed to him or his agencies without independent verification. He frames the broader argument around maintaining a rules-based international order and safeguarding transit rights in the Strait of Hormuz, but offers no data on trade volumes or economic impact beyond qualitative claims that China was Singapore's top merchandise trade partner for more than a decade and remains its largest foreign investor.
items.title: Singapore-China JCBC to advance innovation partnership

items.summary: The Bombay High Court declined to direct Meta Platforms Inc to restore the Facebook and Instagram accounts of digital advertising agency Blink Digital India Pvt Ltd, which had been disabled in August over alleged policy violations. Justice Sandeep Marne rejected the company's plea for interim relief on November 20, citing prima facie material that it sought to attract advertisers by promising services breaching Meta's policies, including 'ban-free' accounts and unlimited spending limits. The court found no right of the plaintiff to insist on using Meta's platforms and held that disabling the accounts was justified to protect users and prevent unfair competitive advantage. Blink Digital had approached the High Court after Meta disabled its four Business Manager accounts on [d1: August 4], along with around [q1: 9,000 advertising] accounts and other business assets; it argued Meta gave no specific reasons or proper opportunity to challenge and allegedly provided inconsistent explanations. The court noted Blink's own submissions showed that around [q2: 500 advertising] accounts were suspended in February [d2: 2026], followed by another [q3: 140 between] May and July, interpreting the agency's repeated offers to remove non-compliant clients as awareness of its violations. The court also rejected a claim that procedural lapses under the Information Technology Rules entitled Blink to immediate restoration. While refusing outright relief, it permitted Blink to approach Meta afresh with an assurance of compliance, directing Meta to consider and communicate within two weeks. As interim protection, Meta was ordered not to delete or destroy the agency's data until its request is decided; this ends if Blink does not approach Meta within four weeks or if the request is rejected. The company has sought Rs [q4: 1,000 crore] in damages.
items.title: Bombay HC Refuses To Order Meta To Restore Blink Digital's Facebook And Instagram Accounts

items.summary: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade agreement, concluding roughly ten years of negotiations with Southeast Asia's biggest economy. The deal removes almost all tariffs between the two sides: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it provides access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries; for Indonesia, it eases exports of palm oil, textiles, and footwear just before its current EU trade preferences expire on January 1st. Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto discussed the deal.
items.title: EU-Indonesia Trade Deal Signed After Decade of Negotiations

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor publicly praised 'Operation Monsoon Thunder,' a joint Indo-US crackdown on transnational drug trafficking. On X, both officials framed the operation as evidence of deepening bilateral cooperation: Shah described the arrests and seizures across India and the US as proof of their partnership's strength while reaffirming Prime Minister Narendra Modi's zero-tolerance policy aimed at preventing any narcotics from entering or leaving Indian borders; Gor called it a 'great example' of US-India collaboration in action. The operation reportedly resulted in six individuals being arrested across four Indian cities, with coordination between India's Narcotics Control Bureau and the US Drug Enforcement Administration credited for disrupting the trafficking network. No quantitative details on seizure volumes were provided by either official.
items.title: Shah and Gor praise Operation Monsoon Thunder narcotics bust

items.summary: The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday after nearly 10 years of negotiations, framing it as one of the bloc's most ambitious agreements in Asia. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the two sides together represent [q1: 730 million people]. The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), alongside an additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA), aims to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. Von der Leyen characterized it as keeping doors open while others close theirs amid more difficult trade with China and the US. About [q2: 98%] of EU exports to Indonesia will have tariffs removed, and European companies could save more than [q3: €600 million] (around [q4: $658 million]) per year. Indonesian Economic Affairs Minister Airlangga Hartarto said the deal benefits his country's main exports—palm oil, footwear, and textiles—and noted that palm oil and deforestation had been major negotiation stumbling blocks, with the agreement including sustainability cooperation mechanisms and a dedicated palm oil protocol. The EU parliament is expected to approve it while Indonesia completes ratification so it can enter into force in [d1: 2027].
items.title: EU and Indonesia Sign Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement

items.summary: The article argues that Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, version [q3: 14], can serve as an alternative to driving for people who cannot fully drive themselves. The author recounts riding his own Tesla Model Y with FSD V14 after a shoulder replacement and arm sling, describing the car navigating from his garage to Vasa Fitness without any intervention on his part. He cites several situations where he believes FSD could allow continued or improved mobility: his daughter's ex-partner who has Parkinson's tremors in his hands; elderly drivers whose ability to navigate may decline with age, including a woman of [q5: 94] years old driving to church with FSD V14; and the author's own daughter recovering from a compound wrist fracture after an accident. He also notes that supervising FSD is easier than one-armed driving for someone like himself, mentions that driving with six cameras ([q6: 6]) may be better than human vision alone, and describes his recent [q7: 1500]-mile trip from Wisconsin to Utah in a Model Y with FSD V14 during which the system failed for about [q8: 500] miles. The author frames Tesla as offering the best automatic-driving hardware available in the US at this time, noting that Tesla began delivering cars with Hardware V4 (HW4) in mid-2023 ([d2]), and contrasts it with Rivian's sensor suite of [q10: 11] cameras and five radar sensors. He attributes a claim to Musk that FSD would prevent [q18: 90%] of traffic deaths if true, though this is presented as an unverified assertion rather than established fact.
items.title: Tesla FSD V14 as a Mobility Option for Drivers With Handicaps and Physical Limitations

items.summary: India and Canada completed their sixth round of face-to-face negotiations on a proposed bilateral Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in New Delhi from November 11-20, with commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal reviewing progress alongside Canadian vice minister Glenn Purves. Sources close to the talks said near consensus was reached across several chapters and some were concluded, covering trade in goods, services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property, and investment promotion; the Indian delegation led by chief negotiator Brij Mohan Mishra faced off against Canadian chief negotiator Mary-Catherine Speirs. The commerce ministry characterized the round as constructive with both sides making progress toward concluding within ambitious timelines set by leaders, while reaffirming a commitment to an agreement that benefits farmers, industries, businesses, and MSMEs in both countries. Both partners plan to continue virtual engagement ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's proposed December 11-12 visit to Canada, during which they may announce tangible progress on trade, investment, energy cooperation, technology, security, and people-to-people ties; separately, the two nations are exploring a two-way energy supply chain in which India would import Canadian oil and gas while sending refined petroleum products back. The report relies on unnamed sources requesting anonymity for details about the talks' outcome and Modi's visit specifics, so no concrete agreement or final terms were confirmed.
items.title: India and Canada Conclude Sixth Round of CEPA Trade Negotiations

items.summary: In a country where roughly [q1: 80%] of people are under 40, Nigerian politics remains dominated by older figures. Since civilian rule began in [d1: 1999], the youngest president elected was Goodluck Jonathan at 53; current president Bola Tinubu is 74 and would be [q2: 79] after a second term, while challengers Atiku Abubakar (79) and Peter Obi (65) are also considerably older. Among the [q4: 18 presidential candidates], only one - Moses Olusoji Adebisi at 35 - is under [q5: 40]. Youth mobilisation has repeatedly surfaced, from EndSars protests in [d2: 2020] to Obi's 'Obedients' movement, but translating enthusiasm into voting has proven difficult. Voter registration rose by [q7: 10 million] to over [q8: 103 million], yet enrolment of those under 35 fell sharply; young people now make up just [q9: 29%] of registered voters, down from [q10: 40%] in [d3: 2023]. High costs further block participation - presidential candidates were permitted to spend up to [q11: 5bn naira] ([q12: £2.8m]; [q13: $3.7m]) for the [d5: 2023] elections, and major parties set nomination fees at [q14: 100m] naira ([q15: $74,000]; [q16: £56,000]). The barriers extend to the legislature too: none of Nigeria's [q17: 109 senators] is under 40, and only [q18: 14] of the [q19: 360 members] of the House of Representatives fall into that age group. Analysts attribute this to both financial constraints and a cultural reluctance among young people to pursue top political positions.
items.title: Nigeria's young majority stays out of elections despite youth-led movements

items.summary: Anindya Banerjee, Head of Commodity, Currency and Rate Derivatives at Kotak Neo, identified $3,500 as the first important support level for gold (within a broader zone of $3,400-$3,500), while silver's next major support sits at $38-$39 an ounce. items.summary: Tasmanian authorities report that an on-duty police officer was shot and a man died nearby during two firearm incidents at the Whitemark police station on Flinders Island. The officer, who was working when he was shot around 9:45pm Saturday night [q1], is in serious but stable condition after being treated at Royal Hobart hospital. Police discovered the body of a man believed to be in his mid-20s with a gunshot wound on Walker Street near the station and stated that they believe the two incidents are linked and have been safely contained. Whitemark has about 300 people [q2] per the 2021 census, while Flinders Island's total population is fewer than 1,000 [q3]. Extra police resources, including forensic and uniformed officers, have been deployed to the island as investigators seek information such as CCTV or dashcam footage. This marks the second shooting of an on-duty officer in Tasmania within 18 months; a Tasmanian officer was killed in June 2025 while executing a court-issued warrant to repossess a residence, and that occupant pleaded guilty to murder.
items.title: Man found dead on Flinders Island linked to shooting of police officer in Tasmania

items.summary: Men's grooming in India is expanding beyond razors and deodorants into products targeting specific skin concerns, with the men's skincare market estimated at ₹6,514 crore in 2026 and projected to reach ₹9,957 crore by 2035 per Reed Intelligence. The shift is reflected across multiple measures: premium men's grooming regimens have grown more than two-and-a-half times from a year ago; Amazon.in reports men's grooming growing 1.6X year-on-year while men's skincare searches entered its top beauty searches for the first time, up 4X year-on-year; and KT Men, which launched in March 2026, has seen orders across haircare, face care, and body care grow 18% month-on-month since launch with sales around 3,000 pieces a day. The change is attributed to men becoming more informed about ingredients and specific needs, increasingly influenced by creators and social media, with adoption growing in tier-2 and tier-3 cities beyond metros.
items.title: India's men are getting serious about skincare

items.summary: Dandruff affects roughly half of the world's population, according to research published this year, though experts still debate its exact cause. Dr Carolyn Goh of UCLA Health describes it as a chronic but manageable condition that comes and goes. Dermatologists classify dandruff as a mild form of seborrheic dermatitis, an inflammatory skin condition concentrated on the scalp rather than elsewhere on the body; Dr Adam Friedman notes possible triggers include overgrowth of the oil-loving yeast Malassezia, increased oil production, and inflammation, while it remains unclear which factor initiates the process. These elements can disrupt the scalp's microbiome, damage the skin barrier, and produce flaking, itching, and greasy scaling, per dermatologist Dr Oyetewa Asempa. Seborrheic dermatitis tends to appear most often in babies—where it is called cradle cap—and in adolescents and older adults, according to the American Academy of Dermatology. Most cases can be treated or prevented with over-the-counter shampoos containing selenium sulfide, pyrithione zinc, or ketoconazole; Dr Friedman says these ingredients target the yeast, oil, and skin cell buildup on the scalp. Severe seborrheic dermatitis may require prescription treatments such as stronger shampoo, antifungal cream or foam, topical corticosteroids to reduce inflammation, oral antifungals, or an enzyme-inhibiting medication that drives inflammation, per Dr Goh; Dr Asempa adds a dermatologist visit when the condition is severe. Other conditions can mimic dandruff: psoriasis, a chronic autoimmune disease causing rapid skin cell turnover and plaques anywhere on the body including the scalp with flaking, burning, itching, and hair loss (treatable with topical steroids or systemic medications per Dr Starling Haynes); allergic contact dermatitis from an irritant in hair products that typically resolves once exposure stops; tinea capitis—ringworm—a contagious fungal infection common among children causing itchiness and patchy hair loss treated usually with oral antifungals; and scarring alopecia, which causes scaling around follicles plus flaking, redness, itching, and permanent hair loss. Management begins with washing the scalp more frequently to remove oil buildup rather than less often in response to perceived dryness, Dr Goh advises, along with over-the-counter shampoo massaged into the scalp for a few minutes before rinsing; avoiding fragranced products or gritty scrubs that can damage the skin barrier and cause irritation is also recommended. If symptoms persist after about a month of dandruff shampoo use—or if hair loss, scalp pain, or pustules appear—consultation with a dermatologist is warranted, as only an in-person evaluation can confirm the underlying cause; Dr Goh emphasizes that dandruff remains a chronic issue requiring ongoing management even when well controlled. The article originally appeared in The New York Times.
items.title: What Causes Dandruff and Other Flaky Scalp Conditions

items.summary: UN climate negotiations at Cop31 reached a standstill on Saturday night in Antalya, Turkey, after the fortnight-long summit overran without resolution and delegates grew increasingly frustrated. The co-conveners of the dual presidency—Australia's Chris Bowen and Turkey's Murat Kurum—held meetings with many countries until late evening as talks stalled. Key sticking points included a loose coalition of about [q1: 130 countries] insisting on including a reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels in the final outcome, alongside demands by developing countries for more climate finance to adapt to worsening impacts. Maina Talia of Tuvalu called the fossil fuel language 'a red line,' while campaigners blamed progress failures on fossil fuel interests and rich countries' failure to deliver promised funding. Other disagreements centered on carbon capture and storage technology and a target to derive [q2: 35%] of the world's energy from electricity by [d1: 2035], with Saudi Arabia seeking strong recommendations for CCS in the final 'cover decision.' Talks were scheduled to end Friday evening but continued into Sunday, with a formal plenary meeting planned for [q3: 9am] local time. The fossil fuel transition language was agreed at Cop28 in Dubai in [d2: 2023], and one possible next step under consideration could force an open meeting where Saudi Arabia would have to publicly state its opposition, though this risks collapsing the talks.
items.title: Climate talks stall in Turkey as countries weigh showdown with Saudi Arabia over fossil fuel phaseout

items.summary: Responding to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's question at a FICCI annual meeting about why companies are not creating jobs or raising salaries despite tax relief, Vedanta Group chairman Anil Agarwal offered three major proposals for boosting employment and economic growth. He claimed that privatizing government-owned firms in natural resources, energy, and manufacturing could increase production up to 10 times while generating millions of new jobs through support to MSMEs. Agarwal attached two conditions to privatization: no layoffs of employees and a tripling of employment, citing airports, ports, airlines, telecom, and metals as sectors where private companies have already tripled or quadrupled job numbers. He suggested privatization could occur by selling shares to private firms or distributing them among the public, using proceeds to reduce debt and increase infrastructure investment. His second proposal called for self-certification to eliminate lengthy approval processes when starting new industries, with the government setting easy rules and ensuring compliance through audits. The third suggestion encouraged small startups in mineral exploration—starting from around ₹5 crore of capital—to explore minerals, metals, and hydrocarbons and sell their findings to companies like ONGC or Hindustan Zinc, noting that current arrangements give the government rights over discovered resources. Agarwal argued that making privatization, self-certification, and exploration a national campaign could increase employment, raise incomes, and strengthen the rupee.
items.title: Anil Agarwal Proposes Privatization and Other Reforms to Boost Jobs After Modi's Query on Employment

An annual Electrek post, updated on [q1: 21NOV]2026 and maintained since [d1: 2024], argues that electrification suits sparsely populated areas at least as well as cities. The author frames the argument around seven points rather than a single headline figure, so no one reading dominates the item. On fuel costs, citing a Rural Climate Partnership study attributed to Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura of the Union of Concerned Scientists (whose 2021 outline is referenced), rural drivers reportedly spend an average of [q6: 44%] more than city dwellers, while the top [q7: 3.6%] — “supermilers” — could save over [q8: $4,000] annually by switching to electric fuel. On vehicle availability, the post contrasts the EV market of [d2: 2021] with that of [q9: 2027], noting affordable options below a [q10: $50,000] half-ton pickup are emerging from Ford and Slate. Charging access is described as limited — only about [q12: 45%] of rural counties have DC fast charging — but home charging is presented as the real advantage, with more than [q13: 80%] of rural households having a driveway or garage suitable for overnight Level [q14: 2] charging and many already holding a [q15: 240V] outlet. On resilience, EVs are said to power refrigerators, freezers, well pumps, and lights through vehicle-to-home systems, with Ford’s F-150 Lightning and Tesla’s Cybertruck cited as examples; the post claims such energy can be “[q20: 100%] Made in the USA.” On affordability, it notes working-class buyers once expected a pickup under [q18: $50,000], now achievable via lease deals, tax incentives, and Ford Pro/TRC funding. On longevity, an author-covered [d5: 2019] Chevy Bolt reportedly logged over [q22: 470,000 miles], while Ford data is cited showing battery packs retaining more than [q23: 90%] of health after [q24: 100,000 miles]; the first modern high-voltage EV (the Prius) reportedly launched in [d6: 1996] as a [d7: 1997] model. A commenter from rural Australia adds that his ~[q26: 164km] ([q27: 100miles]) shopping trip and rooftop solar make an EV “a no-brainer” there, though he notes local conservatism about range anxiety and battery replacement fears. The piece also promotes EnergySage for solar quotes, claiming users can save [q28: 20]-30% versus going it alone.

The item is explicitly opinion-driven rather than evidence-led; figures are attributed to the Rural Climate Partnership study (via Pinto de Moura), Ford data, and a single author-covered vehicle. The “100% Made in the USA” energy claim rests on wind/solar expansion without quantification, and no numerical comparison of EV versus gas total cost is provided — only that EVs can be had for less than comparable models via financing.

No chart was constructed because the item presents seven distinct qualitative reasons rather than a single measurable quantity or time series; any figures are isolated claims from different sources with mismatched denominators, so no useful comparison could be supported.
items.title: 7 reasons rural drivers should embrace EVs in 2027 (Electrek)

items.summary: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, a subsidiary of the Mahindra Group, won the 'Clean Our Air' category at Prince William's Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai. The award recognizes its electric three-wheeler for reducing pollution and creating employment opportunities. Along with the prize, the company received a grant of 10 lakh British pounds (over ₹12 crore). To date, Mahindra has sold over 4 lakh electric last-mile vehicles in India, which have collectively traveled more than 9 billion kilometers. According to the company's figures, using these vehicles helped prevent nearly 1.85 lakh metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions. The Earthshot Prize was launched by Prince William in [d1: 2020] to encourage innovations addressing environmental challenges; this year five winners were selected, each receiving a prize money of 10 lakh pounds. Mahindra's MD and CEO Suman Mishra received the award from cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, with Prince William and Princess Catherine in attendance. According to Suman Mishra, lower running costs have played the most important role in adopting electric vehicles; although the initial price of an electric three-wheeler is higher, drivers can save over time due to cheaper operation compared to petrol or diesel. The company has also trained 500 women [q11: 500] in driving and repairing electric three-wheelers.
items.title: Mahindra Wins Earthshot Prize for Electric Three-Wheeler; Receives Over ₹12 Crore Grant

The International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook warns that global electricity demand from information technology is set to rise by more than [q1: 10,000 TWh] over the next ten years, requiring urgent grid upgrades. The IEA cautioned that while AI may eventually help with energy efficiency and grid optimization, surging data center demand is currently amplifying strains in some markets and supply chains, stressing the importance of keeping electricity affordable as pro-transition governments expand renewable share.

The financial burden falls unevenly: a Cornell University study found U.S. data center operators paid only [q2: 38%] of grid connection infrastructure costs, with operators paying $[q3: 3.12 billion] and households covering the remaining $[q4: 5.13 billion]. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal reported some [q5: 58 GW] in new data centers under construction across roughly [q6: 577 locations], representing demand about six times New York City's peak electricity use.

Grid investment needs are enormous globally. The European Union plans to double cross-border interconnectors at a cost of [q7: 584 billion euros] until [d1: 2030], equivalent to $[q8: 641 billion]. This clashes with affordability goals, since utilities and governments cannot absorb the costs without spreading them. The article notes that requiring data center operators to fully fund their own energy supply is politically contentious because AI has yet to deliver comparable returns.

The piece attributes all figures as reported claims from its sources (IEA, Cornell University study, WSJ) rather than established fact, and frames opposition—such as Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's proposed moratorium—as campaign statements. It also lists unrelated market readings: Europe has already drained [q9: 11%] of its summer gas injections.
items.title: AI Boom Forces Massive Investment in Power Grids Worldwide

items.summary: President Meredith Whittaker of Signal framed operating systems that integrate agentic AI as an 'existential threat' to the app's privacy guarantees, arguing that Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS let AI agents scan on-screen content—capturing sensitive data outside Signal's control. Building on its existing default block of screenshots in the Windows app, Signal announced Friday restrictions for Android and iOS; users can disable these settings at their own discretion, which Whittaker warned would 'break our privacy guarantees.' She also acknowledged the measure as an incomplete solution that does not address other ways AI agents might access application data. The text offers no quantitative evidence to support its claims.
items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots amid concerns over agentic-AI surveillance

items.summary: A security incident at Rackspace's cloud platform allowed attackers to reach sensitive data in customer clusters, according to a disclosure obtained by BleepingComputer. Hackers accessed parts of the Rackspace Spot platform on November 17 using leaked credentials and were able to act as legitimate users within some organizations, creating pods in Kubernetes clusters, reading Kubernetes Secrets (which store passwords, authentication tokens, and API keys), and listing nodes and volumes. The intrusion occurred between approximately 00:20 and 22:00 UTC on that date; Rackspace learned of it the next day after a customer report and confirmed the affected organization's involvement same-day. Because attackers could read any Secret stored in an affected user's clusters as well as Spot API tokens or refresh tokens held by that user, customers were instructed to reissue their Spot API tokens, replace automation refresh tokens, download fresh Kubernetes configuration files, rotate cluster-secret credentials, and review logs from databases, container registries, Git repositories, cloud storage, and third-party services dating back to November 17. Rackspace reported indicators of compromise including the IP address 23.224.79.106, an IP range of 23.224.0.0/15, and suspicious Kubernetes pod/object prefixes (i1, glm-, probe). The company said it had revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed unauthorized pods, rotated keys, and strengthened access controls and monitoring; the breach also caused an extended outage of the Rackspace Spot administration console that temporarily blocked customers from managing clusters or rotating credentials. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and Chief Growth Officer of Platform9 (which co-developed Rackspace Spot), said the team deliberately disabled access while securing infrastructure to best protect users; service was fully restored on November 21. BleepingComputer asked how many customers were affected and whether customer data was stolen but received no response.
items.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets

items.summary:
A 16-year-old Colorado boy, Landon Tresp, was chatting online with another teenager when she revealed that she had run away from home and was being held against her will hundreds of miles away. She said she had been missing for more than a year and believed police were no longer looking for her. After about two weeks of conversation, he told his mother Khristina on 31 October; the FBI later reported the rescue occurred roughly 24 hours after Landon first alerted her.

Khristina contacted the girl directly through Discord, learned she was in Oregon but did not know the exact location, and asked her to find a document with a full name. Using tax and property records plus real estate photos, Khristina identified the address where the girl was held; the girl confirmed it before asking that no one be told until her captor left.

The alleged captor, Adam Hunter Harmel, reportedly met Jenny on social media in May 2025, offered money to help him reach Oregon after picking her up in Utah, then drove her across state lines and kept her confined. According to the criminal complaint, he allegedly forced her into his bed with a knife nearby, gave her only a wifi-connected phone unable to make calls, became violent and sexually assaulted her, and removed her braces so she would not be identifiable.

While Harmel was away from home, officers staged outside at street level while Khristina coached Jenny through the escape; law enforcement reportedly relayed how close they were. The FBI monitored their call once he left in the morning, and state troopers met Jenny as she fled to safety. Harmel is now in federal custody charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

The account rests on screenshots of communications shared by the family and a photo matching the complaint; BBC protected the girl's identity, which it called "Jenny." The defendant did not comment, though local Oregon media reported he was also accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old before Jenny disappeared. Jenny remains in contact with Khristina and Landon but has not met them in person.
items.title: Teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl

items.summary: A study published in PLOS One by psychologist Anna Lena Dueren of Germany analyzed responses from more than 15,000 people about memorable hugs. Nearly 70 per cent could recall a hug that left them with positive feelings, most often because it offered comfort, support or understanding. The perception of hugs depends on gender and attachment style: those scoring higher in avoidant attachment were less likely to remember positive hugs, while those with anxious attachment had a greater likelihood of doing so. Dr Gail Saltz, not involved in the study, said these results align with known attachment dynamics—those seeking reassurance may find comfort in hugs, while those uncomfortable with intimacy may feel smothered. Among all reasons cited for remembering a hug, arousal was mentioned least by participants who were mostly women; men were more likely than women to remember hugs as physically arousing, though the survey did not specify whether this meant sexual arousal. The study drew on data from the Touch Test worldwide survey but included only subjects living in the United Kingdom without chronic health conditions. Limitations include a lack of geographic diversity and self-selected participants recruited through public broadcasting and other media who may have been especially interested in touch, as well as more than 70 per cent being female, which could skew results.
items.title: Attachment Style and Gender Shape How People Remember Hugs

items.summary: Analysts say that although Donald Trump has framed his three summits with Xi Jinping this year as a victory and praised the accompanying fanfare, he has gained little concretely from them. In contrast, analysts argue Xi has strengthened his position on the world stage: after emerging from a global gathering in China as a statesman capable of convening the first China-U.S.-Russia summit, Beijing is holding a fragile trade truce with Washington in what it considers favorable terms even as the U.S. takes a harder line. The analysts' assessment rests only on public announcements, which they note show few concrete gains for Trump; no specific deals or measurable outcomes were detailed beyond these characterizations of relative positioning.
items.title: Trump's Xi Summits Yield Little for Washington While Beijing Strengthens Its Position

The interview was framed around what President Xi Jinping gained from a notably warm personal greeting—described as a 'bear hug'—from Trump during their meeting in Shenzhen. Asked whether she might attend the 2032 Brisbane Olympics — where Australia will host as Fraser was also central to Sydney 2000 — she said she would love to be there to support Australian athletes, noting that some competitors at the reunion are aged 95 and 99, which motivates her despite turning 89. At Melbourne in 1956, Fraser won gold in the 100-metre freestyle (q5) and was part of the women's 4x100 freestyle relay team that also took gold (q6); she became one of only four swimmers to win an individual event at three successive Olympics. She described how winning there changed her perspective on global competition, framing Melbourne as a landmark for Australian sport after World War Two and expressing hope that Brisbane will outshine Sydney.
items.title: Dawn Fraser inspired by 1956 Melbourne Olympics reunion to attend 2032 Brisbane Games

Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Malik invoked the layered history of Delhi's Purana Qila while addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, framing cultural diversity and shared heritage as foundations for dialogue amid strained New Delhi–Islamabad ties. Speaking Saturday at a session titled 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions,' chaired by Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Malik described the fort as built on one wall but shaped by two rival rulers: Mughal emperor Humayun, who laid its foundation drawing on his Central Asian Timurid lineage, and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri, who further constructed it after defeating Humayun. He characterised this as 'two rivals' contributing to 'one trench,' using the monument's overlapping histories to argue that dialogue requires distinct identities exchanging ideas freely.

Malik made these remarks at a three-day forum inaugurated Friday evening by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and hosted jointly by India's Culture Ministry and External Affairs Ministry from November 20–22. His visit marks his first trip to India, occurring after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack; when asked whether the event could improve bilateral relations, he said discussions were taking place in a 'multilateral context.'

The venue was selected to showcase Delhi's civilisational heritage and historical layers. Humayun founded the fort as part of his planned capital Dinpanah, with construction continued by Sher Shah Suri after seizing control; the site is also associated with Indraprastha from the Mahabharata. As part of the forum, delegates viewed 'Astitva -- The Essence of our Existence,' an exhibition tracing Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE.

Shekhawat described shared cultural heritage as a bridge connecting SCO countries and called for cooperation through dialogue, institutional partnerships, and cultural exchanges. Modi characterised Purana Qila as 'extraordinary heritage' whose history scholars say stretches back thousands of years to the Mahabharata era. On Saturday, participants also visited an exhibition at the Qila Rai Pithora complex in south Delhi.

The article presents Malik's remarks as his own framing and attributes historical claims about Humayun, Sher Shah Suri, Indraprastha, and the archaeological dating range to their respective sources rather than treating them as established fact.
items.title: Pakistani minister invokes Humayun and Sher Shah Suri at SCO forum in Delhi

items.summary: A new report from Ember Energy, titled Harnessing the Winds, argues that wind power represents a major missed opportunity for energy security and emissions goals. The analysis finds that adding wind to solar and battery storage makes firm renewable power cheaper because the two sources produce at different times of day and seasons. Specifically, 90 percent of electricity demand can be met more cheaply when wind complements solar and batteries on overcast days and winter days with short daylight hours; under this scenario, the median cost per megawatt hour falls by more than 18 percent, from $105 to $86. The remaining 10 percent of electricity that these three sources cannot meet would be supplied by gas or diesel. Expanding wind deployment also improves energy security and grid resilience by reducing the risk of a simultaneous solar and wind lull, known as Dunkelflaute. However, benefits are uneven: near the equator, where seasonal solar fluctuations are minimal, adding wind has little impact on costs, while in cash-strapped regions like sub-Saharan Africa, deploying wind remains prohibitively expensive. Wind power has expanded more slowly than solar and batteries partly because turbines improve at a slower rate due to challenges testing new models under constantly changing atmospheric conditions.

items.summary: The Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) has urged the 8th Central Pay Commission, chaired by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, to overhaul promotion rules for central government employees and recommend that minimum qualifying service be fixed between one and four years depending on cadre requirements. In a November 20 letter addressed to the chairperson, FNPO Secretary General Sivaji Vasireddy sought review of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) office memorandum issued September 20, 2022, arguing that its widely varying qualifying-service periods have caused prolonged career stagnation and vacant supervisory posts. Under the current framework, promotion from Level 6 to Level 11 requires as much as 12 years of service; transitions between Levels 4-6, 6-10 and 11-13 require 10 years each; while moves such as Level 2 to Level 4 and Level 6 to Level 9 require eight years. In contrast, some promotions under the same framework allow just one to three years of qualifying service. FNPO contends that lengthy timelines have left positions like Lower Selection Grade, Higher Selection Grade, supervisory roles in postal and Railway Mail Service offices, Senior Superintendent posts and director-level jobs vacant for extended periods, increasing workload on existing officers and weakening supervision. The federation also cited career stagnation, delayed financial benefits and reduced morale among employees, arguing that qualifying service should reflect post responsibilities rather than pay-level differences. Beyond administrative strain, it requested safeguards for current staff during the transition to a revised framework along with periodic reviews of promotion rules' impact on vacancies.

items.summary: The Bell Canada AI Fabric data centre near Regina is billed as Canada's largest private-sector capital investment, but its environmental footprint extends beyond the facility itself. Once fully operational it will require up to [q1: 1.2 gigawatts] of electricity, split between a dedicated onsite bring-your-own-power scheme providing [q3: 900 megawatts] and the provincial grid supplying only [q5: 300 megawatts]. Bell Canada says it will use energy responsibly without competing for local power resources. The company claims its own cooling uses a sealed, closed-loop water system paired with an air-cooled heat-rejection system that would not touch groundwater or municipal supply; however, this accounts only for the data centre's direct water use and ignores the water needed to generate the electricity it consumes. A PhD researcher studying integrated water management in the Assiniboine River basin explains that most power generation remains highly water-intensive: SaskPower's 2025-26 annual report indicates around [q4: 25%] of Saskatchewan's capacity comes from coal-fired plants, and if the grid allocates [q5: 300 megawatts] to Bell Canada, cooling water will still be needed elsewhere. Because southern Saskatchewan's coal plants sit far from Regina, this demand would shift rather than disappear, potentially increasing total ecosystem withdrawal away from the data centre site; nuclear reactors planned along Rafferty Reservoir and refurbishments of Poplar River, Shand and Boundary Dam would face similar cooling-water needs. The researcher also notes that if natural gas is used instead—following Alberta's path—the province would need to import most gas from Alberta given its limited local production, adding water for drilling, extraction, processing and delivery; meanwhile seasonal swings in Assiniboine basin precipitation versus fixed industrial demand complicate regional water balance during droughts. Prime Minister Mark Carney has built unusually broad support by positioning himself as Canada's counterweight to Trump, winning backing across francophone Quebec and conservative Alberta and turning his Liberals' minority government into a majority in April. Analysts attribute this goodwill partly to the tense circumstances of his rise: Scott Reid describes it as unprecedented because he draws support from both left and right, while Philippe Fournier dismisses current seat projections as implausibly large. This political capital has enabled Carney to pursue an ambitious agenda with little resistance—approving a Pacific oil pipeline framed as national sovereignty rather than ideology, running deficits far larger than any previous leader contemplated (a C$140bn/£74bn spending announcement in early November and a business tax credit costing C$36bn/£19bn over five years), introducing Bill C-39 to fast-track infrastructure at the expense of environmental reviews despite warnings from nearly 60 Royal Society scientists, cancelling the consumer carbon tax and pausing EV sales targets as Canada falls short of its 2030 or 2035 emissions goals, abandoning thermal coal export work begun in 2024, and proposing to sell parts of four major airports. Critics warn that this tolerance is tied to Trump-era anxieties: Julia Levin notes Canadians have granted grace while overlooking policies at odds with Canadian values, and Reid questions whether Carney's domestic appeal can survive if the trade war ends or Trump disappears—suggesting his popularity may not be durable once the exceptional circumstances fade.
items.title: Mark Carney's popularity lets him push controversial policies amid Trump tensions

items.summary: At age 80, Paul Schrader is embracing AI across scriptwriting, acting, and visual effects—contrasting sharply with much of the industry. He told the Guardian he sees no future for humanity as AI advances: “I don’t see a place for Homo sapiens in the larger scheme of things.” While directors like Steven Spielberg and Christopher Nolan express scepticism, Schrader is actively using the technology; Sag-Aftra recently required producers to show an AI performer adds significant value over a live actor, and the Academy banned AI actors and screenplays from Oscars this year—both moves he dismissed as desperate. For his new horror-thriller The Doors of Perception with San Francisco studio Fable, Schrader relied on AI to judge how graphic psychedelic hallucinations should be rendered. He also screen-tested AI actors for Three Guns at Dawn after Black actors declined roles in a story about three Black brothers; the script generated more than 40 scenes and he found it spooking when AI produced stage directions resembling his own style, prompting him to “pull the needle out of my arm.” Schrader frames this as opening a monster’s cage without a leash. The article notes audiences may feel let down by films made with AI, though no data on reception is provided.
items.title: Paul Schrader embraces AI filmmaking at 80 amid Hollywood resistance

items.summary:
International human rights judge Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong dedication to international law and global justice. Sam Naidu, author of 'Navi Pillay: Realising Human Rights for All,' spoke about the activist he profiled after interviewing her in Switzerland in 2009 with access to her personal archives in South Africa. He described her as down-to-earth, no-nonsense, generous, and exuding strength, integrity, and intelligence, noting that a steely grit she detected beneath her warmth appears to have strengthened over time, citing her stance against Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Naidu chose Pillay—whom he shares an Indian diasporic community with in Durban—as his subject because she was an inspirational black woman who overcame structural barriers to become a pioneer in human rights law.

Pillay (born Navanethem Pillay) has Tamil ancestry; her grandparents were indentured labourers brought from India by ship in the late 19th century to work on sugarcane fields in KwaZulu-Natal. She was born in 1941 and grew up as the fifth of eight children in a working-class home in Clairwood, Durban; her father drove a bus and fished for extra income while stressing education's value.

She began her career fighting human rights under apartheid South Africa: she set up a law practice in 1967 (the first black woman to do so), defended ANC member Phyllis Naidoo, obtained legal representation for political prisoners at Robben Island prison in 1973, and co-founded the Advice Desk for Abused Women in 1986. Formal apartheid ended with South Africa's first democratic elections in 1994; Pillay was recommended by Nelson Mandela as the first black female judge in the Supreme Court in 1995.

She joined the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda that same year, was promoted to its judge president in 1999, moved to the International Criminal Court in The Hague, and became UN High Commissioner for Human Rights in 2008. Forbes Magazine named her one of the world's 100 most powerful women in August 2009 at number 64, making her the second African ever on that list.

Naidu credited Pillay with transforming international human rights law through her interventions at the Rwanda tribunal, which became the first court to hold that sexual violence can be an act of genocide. On May 30, 1996, in the case against Jean-Paul Akayesu (charged with fifteen counts including genocide but not sexual violence), Pillay prompted the prosecution to indict on rape charges, leading to a finding that rape may constitute genocide under certain circumstances; this provision was later incorporated into modern international criminal law. Naidu called it 'rarely [a] feminist victory with more real, material impact.'

Naidu acknowledged that Pillay's lifelong quest for justice has won her enemies who belittle or criticize her methods, though he found the ideals she adheres to hard to fault.

The article notes historical surprises as caveats: Jan Smuts (a white supremacist) left his lasting legacy in the UN Charter preamble; Nelson Mandela was not expected to become South Africa's president by 1963; and it is difficult to have predicted that Pillay would win the Nobel Peace Prize. Naidu framed her enduring question—originally asked as a six-year-old when she witnessed an unjust court process—as now global: 'Where is justice for each and every one of us?'
items.title: Biographer Sam Naidu on Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize win and career

items.summary: Mexican authorities captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” overnight in the state of Sinaloa. He was one of [q1: 10] FBI most wanted fugitives and a top leader of the Beltrán Leyva criminal organization, sought for trafficking drugs to the United States and illegally carrying firearms. Authorities said they used stealth and surprise, establishing a security perimeter around his building before armed forces entered a home after he was attacked with guns and explosives from likely cartel operatives. The capture triggered violence in Guasave, including gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and gas stations, and helicopters firing on homes—shows of force common following cartel leader takedowns. Mexican officials said intelligence from the Trump administration helped the operation but provided few details about coordination between the two countries. This comes as President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from President Donald Trump to crack down on cartels; homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office, and she has pursued illegal groups more aggressively than predecessors. The capture follows that of El Mencho, Mexico's most powerful cartel leader, who was killed in February.
items.title: Mexico Detains Cartel Leader 'El Chapo Isidro' in Sinaloa

items.summary: Australia beat England by three wickets to win the first of five T20 internationals on Saturday, November 21, at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Nikhil Chaudhary produced a match-winning performance: taking 2-21 with his leg-spin and scoring [q1: 66] from [q2: 38 balls], which set up Australia's chase of [q3: 188] — a record total at the MCG. Chaudhary fell short, needing [q4: 20 runs off the last two overs], but an England attack missing Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Sonny Baker could not close it out. Sam Curran defended [q5: 11] in the final over before Jack Edwards won it off the penultimate delivery to reach 191-7. Chaudhary — India-born but having arrived on a tourist visa six years ago, staying due to COVID travel restrictions — was named player of the match; his parents had flown from India for their first game watching him play in Australia. The two sides are scheduled to contest the second T20I on Tuesday at Carrara on the Gold Coast south of Brisbane.
items.title: Nikhil Chaudhary's all-round display powers Australia past England in T20I thriller at MCG

items.summary: After a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile and two other objects—believed to be another missile and a jet-powered drone—struck Polish territory on Friday, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Saturday that all allies stand in full solidarity with Poland. The incident occurred while the Coalition of the Willing was conducting military exercises nearby; per TVP reporting, authorities were still assessing circumstances as Rutte called the breach dangerous and unacceptable. Speaking to TVP Info after talks with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Warsaw, Rutte said the response by Polish F-16 fighter jets backed by NATO exemplified how the alliance should work. The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russia timed the incursions to coincide with the drills to test NATO's response and deter support for Ukraine, noting that Polish officials requested additional NATO forces and air defense capabilities—though Warsaw did not invoke Article 4 consultations. These details are drawn from unverified reporting by TVP and assessments attributed to ISW rather than confirmed facts.
items.title: NATO chief says allies stand with Poland after Russian airspace breach

items.summary: Cricket leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal made his political debut on Saturday by joining the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and being named a 'Special Invitee' to the party's newly formed National OBC Morcha executive committee. The BJP announced these appointments as per directions from national president Nitin Nabin, effective immediately; Maurya said they followed instructions from that same source. Chahal will represent Delhi in the wing dedicated to Other Backward Classes, a move expected to strengthen the BJP ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections where OBC voters form a significant bloc. On X on [d1: November 21, 2026], he thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and OBC Morcha national president Amarpal Maurya for the inclusion. The announcement also named seven national vice presidents (Jogen Mohan from Assam, Mamata Mohanta from Odisha, Sangam Lal Gupta from Uttar Pradesh, Babanrao Raoji Chaudhary from Maharashtra, Sat Prakash Rana from Delhi, Arjun Sahni from Bihar, and Sangeeta Balwant Bind from Uttar Pradesh), three national general secretaries (Gajendra Yadav from Delhi, Pramod Madhwaraj from Karnataka, and Lalit Chandrakar from Chhattisgarh), seven additional national secretaries, and 37 members of the national executive committee. Born in [d2: 1990], Chahal is described as the first Indian bowler to take [q2: 400 wickets] in T20 cricket, with best figures of 6/25 against England; Punjab bought him for Rs [q3: 18 crore ahead] of the [d3: 2025] season. He has played county cricket in England and represents Haryana domestically.
items.title: Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP as OBC Morcha 'Special Invitee'

items.summary: A viral video circulating on X after the August 2026 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, purportedly shows Russian President Vladimir Putin extending his hand for a handshake that Chinese President Xi Jinping turns away from, prompting speculation about diplomatic tensions between Beijing and Moscow. The footage is fake: FRANCE 24 traced it via reverse image search to authentic material filmed during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation meeting in Kyrgyzstan in August [d1: 2026], where both leaders clearly shake hands with no indication of a snub, and falsely presented as recent APEC summit footage when original video from that gathering also shows them shaking hands. The creator's post has accumulated more than [q4: 10 million views] and was flagged as AI-generated content; the account describes itself as satire and openly acknowledged producing the clip with Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI.
items.title: Viral AI-Generated Video Depicts Xi Jinping 'Snubbing' Putin at APEC Summit; FRANCE 24 Confirms Footage Is Fake and Misattributed to Recent Meeting

items.summary: The BADBOX malware botnet has returned following last year's disruptions, generating a record 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day through infected Android-based devices. According to HUMAN's Satori researchers, who uncovered and disrupted the latest variant, BADBOX 3.0 had grown into the largest documented ad-fraud operation by daily bid request volume. At its height, BADBOX 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform. Its volume was more than three times that of VASTFLUX, the previous record holder, and represents a larger peak than the last five years' worth of published Satori investigations combined.
items.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking daily ad fraud volume

Cement led with the highest selling at Rs [q4: 8,004 million], followed closely by Hotels, Restaurants & Tourism at Rs [q7: 7,544 million]. Private Banks saw a total of Rs [q10: 7,310 million] in selling.
